paper.title: Stochastic Linear Optimization with Adversarial Corruption

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear optimization with adversarial corruption
unmapped: corruption functions c_t: D -> [-1,1]; C = sum_t max_x |c_t(x)| unknown to the learner
action set D is a d-dimensional polytope
settings.definition_quote: Let $\xSet \subseteq \reals^\dimension$ be a $\dimension$-polytope... $\{\noise_t\}$ a sequence of sub-Gaussian random noise with mean 0 and variance proxy 1... there is an adaptive adversary who may corrupt the observed reward by choosing a corruption function $c_t:D \to [-1, 1]$... The value of $C$ is unknown to the algorithm, which is, in turn, evaluated by pseudo-regret

algorithms.name: SBE with polynomial-time weak Löwner-John ellipsoid (zeta = 2^14 d^6 log(4d log T/delta))

tuning: zeta = 2^14 d^5 log(4 d log T / delta) (as used in the proof)

source.label: thm:final regret
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\confidence$, the regret is bounded by \regret = \bigO{ \frac{\dimension^{2} \corruption \log \horizon}{\truediff} + \frac{\dimension^5 \log (\sfrac{\dimension \log \horizon}{\delta})\log \horizon}{\truediff^2}}.

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret on uncorrupted means, holding w.p. 1-delta. Delta is gap between best and second-best extreme point (Delta_lin). Uses an exact Löwner-John ellipsoid (computation not discussed); the algorithm box sets zeta with d^6 while the proof uses d^5 — inconsistency in paper.

tuning: zeta = 2^14 d^6 log(4 d log T / delta)

source.quote: By plugging the polynomial time algorithm for finding John's ellipsoid from \citet{lovasz1990geometric} into our \Cref{alg:explobycoor}, and setting the parameter $\parameter = 2^{14} \dimension^6 \log (\sfrac{4\dimension \log \horizon}{\delta})$, we have an computationally efficient algorithm whose regret is of $\bigO{\frac{\dimension^{5/2} \corruption \log \horizon}{\truediff} + \frac{\dimension^6 \log (\sfrac{\dimension \log \horizon}{\delta}) \log \horizon}{\truediff^2}}$.

results.notes: Stated in text, not a formal theorem; probability 1-delta stated in the conclusion. Conclusion also says delta=1/T gives expected regret O(d^{5/2} C log T/Delta + d^6 log^2 T/Delta^2) (not recorded separately).
